Using JavaGD is very straightforward and easy. Once you have JavaGD 
installed, and taking that you have an R object on which you can call 
'plot' (called 'plot_object' in the example below), the following code 
should be all you need:

//call the JavaGD library into use
re.eval("library(JavaGD)");
//give the plot its properties
re.eval("JavaGD(name='Thingy to plot', width=800, height=600, ps=12)");
//plot it
re.eval("plot(plot_object)");

Graham

There is no "JGR libraries" -- you either want to use rJava (then just  
do it) or you want to use JGR but then you cannot run your package  
outside of JGR.


> I have 3 jars placed in the "java" folder of the package:

> .jpackage(name="easyfilteR")  .jcall("rif/ 
> RIFFrame","V",method="main",.jnull("[Ljava/lang/String;"))
> }
>

I'm not sure what you're trying to achieve here -- the above is not  
supposed to work. You have it either backwards (.jpackage starts the  
JVM so it should be first -- .jengine needs an already started JVM and  
I hope you know what you're doing since it requires you to have  
working JRI at that point) and as Romain said, you cannot run  
library(JGR) -- it's either a noop if you're inside JGR or it just  
won't do anything useful to you if you are not inside JGR.

If your package hooks into JGR you should use something like this  
instead:

.First.lib <- function(lib, pkg) {
   if (!"JGR" %in% .packages() || !.jfield("org/rosuda/JGR/ 
JGR","Z","STARTED"))
     stop("JGR is not running. This package must be used from JGR.")
   .jpackage(name=pkg, lib.loc=lib)
}

If you don't need JGR, then it should be simply .jpackage(..) and  
that's it.

I hope it helps ...

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Rserve
messages.body_plain:
On Oct 26, 2009, at 7:53 AM, Edzer Pebesma wrote:

> as I've mentioned before, we use Rserve in the INTAMAP.org project  
> to do spatial interpolation of data behind a java/tomcat client  
> interface. A problem we've run into is the following: if the  
> interpolation seems to take long (days...), one often breaks the  
> request to the java client. This however does not terminate the R  
> process. Does Rserve provide the possibility to control this, i.e.  
> stop the Rserve child process, without completely terminating Rserve  
> altogether?
>

You can use sessions for long-term evaluation (see voidEvalDetach).  
Another way is to use the server as the collector of the results form  
children (see control commands in Rserve 0.6). Finally, to kill a  
specific child, send it a a signal (e.g. INT if you calculation checks  
signals or TERM if it doesn't) -- you can do that by calling Sys.getpid 
() in the child first and then using another child instance on the  
same machine to send the signal.

Cheers,
Simon
